text: Sikhism began more than 500 years ago in the Punjab, with the teaching of Guru Nanak.
According to tradition, he said, “There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim”, for God is beyond all divisions.
src: Sikhism began with Guru Nanak’s teaching in the Punjab around 1500
according to the traditional accounts of his life / “There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim”, proclaiming that God is beyond all religious divisions

text: Sikhs believe in one God, found by all people equally, and serve God through honest work and sharing.
The free kitchen of the Golden Temple feeds tens of thousands of people every day, all seated together on the floor.
src: one God, remembered in prayer, served through honest work and sharing, and found by all people equally
The free kitchen (langar) of the Golden Temple at Amritsar serves meals to tens of thousands of people every day / all of them seated together on the floor as equals

text: Guru Gobind Singh, the last of ten human Gurus, founded the Khalsa, a group of initiated Sikhs, in 1699.
Before he died, he said that the holy book, the Guru Granth Sahib, would be the Guru after him.
src: a line of ten human Gurus / under Guru Gobind Singh in 1699, the Khalsa order of initiated Sikhs
before his death in 1708 declared that the Granth would be the Guru after him / The Guru Granth Sahib is the central scripture of Sikhism

text: Sikhs were persecuted by later Mughal rulers, and two Gurus were put to death on the orders of Mughal emperors.
Later, Sikhs built their own empire under Ranjit Singh.
src: Persecuted under the later Mughals / Guru Arjan was executed under the emperor Jahangir / Tegh Bahadur, was executed in Delhi in 1675 on the orders of the emperor Aurangzeb
Sikhs built their own empire under Ranjit Singh

text: Sikhism has no priests: the holy book and the community of Sikhs guide it.
Today 25 to 30 million Sikhs live in the Punjab and around the world.
src: Sikhism has no priesthood. Authority rests with the scripture and with the community gathered in its presence
